audit.whatIsWrong: Chart read Skill / Skill / Skill / Cassiopeia / Skill / Skill / Cassiopeia — it gave Cassiopeia the late game outright. The prose on the same entry says 'Level 1 is his', 'From level 2 the lane flips', 'my clearest lane edge' at 3, and 'This is where I lose the matchup' late.
audit.why: Lane difficulty is a key point and the chart had the two decisive stages backwards: it handed Cassiopeia a late game the page itself says she loses.
audit.corrected: Trundle / Cassiopeia / Cassiopeia / Skill / Skill / Cassiopeia / Trundle in both layers.

audit.whatIsWrong: No cooldown numbers on an entry whose plan is entirely about timing windows against his sustain.
audit.why: Power spikes is a key point; 'chip him before Frozen Domain comes online' and 'he can wall your kite' need durations to be actionable.
audit.corrected: Chomp 3.5s, Pillar of Ice 21s at rank 1 and Subjugate 120/100/80 added where the band allowed. The mirror added Miasma's 24s from the other side.

audit.whatIsWrong: wants.you[1] tells you to 'ground him off a Pillar (E) escape'. Pillar of Ice creates impassable terrain — it is not a movement ability and Grounded does not touch it, and Trundle has no dash at all, so the grounding half of Miasma is worth nothing in this matchup. Separately, spikes[1] and mid both promise Petrifying Gaze 'stuns his all-in' without the facing rule: it stuns only enemies facing Cassiopeia and merely slows anyone with their back turned.
audit.why: Point 4 is the most important point. The page sold Miasma's grounding as a counter to an ability it cannot affect, and sold the level-6 stun as unconditional.
audit.corrected: Grounding stated as dead weight here, with Miasma repositioned as a pure slow zone; Petrifying Gaze's facing condition stated. Both match what the mirror audits/top/trundle__cassiopeia.json concluded from Trundle's side.
sources: champ-data/_kits/trundle.json (E Pillar of Ice, terrain; no dash in kit)
champ-data/_kits/cassiopeia.json (W grounding wording; R facing rule)

audit.whatIsWrong: No anti-heal recommendation, on an entry whose stated losing condition is that he out-heals a full Q-W-E rotation.
audit.why: King's Tribute and Frozen Domain are the reason the poke war fails; Grievous Wounds is the only item answer and it was never named.
audit.corrected: Grievous Wounds folded into the early text.

audit.whatIsWrong: early, mid, late, whys[0] and whys[1] are all written in the first person — 'my Twin Fang treadmill', 'This is where I lose the matchup', 'Level 1 I have one ability'.
audit.why: Every other Cassiopeia entry addresses the player in the second person; this one reads as a different champion narrating.
audit.corrected: Rewritten in second person throughout the strings I touched.
sources: voice used across the rest of champ-data/content/cassiopeia.js

edits.before: Petrifying Gaze (R) stuns him out of his all-in, but it does not stop Subjugate (R) draining your armor/MR onto him — R to survive and disengage, do not R-then-greed a kill.
edits.after: Petrifying Gaze stuns him only if he is facing you, and it never stops Subjugate (R) draining your armor and MR onto him — R to survive the commit, never R-then-greed a kill.

edits.before: Use Miasma (W) to ground him off a Pillar (E) escape and zone the wave — not to chase, since his sustain beats an extended trade
edits.after: Miasma's grounding is dead weight here — he has no dash and Pillar is terrain — so use W purely as a slow zone to buy spacing

edits.before: Level 1 is his — he has Chomp (Q) stealing my attack damage plus a Pillar (E) angle, and that out-trades my single Noxious Blast (Q) before I can stack any poison. From level 2 the lane flips to me: I prime with Q, then chain Twin Fang (E) off the poison for cheap, near-continuous damage and chip him before his Frozen Domain (W) attack-speed-and-heal zone and passive sustain switch on. Do not over-commit for the kill — his whole kit is built to out-heal a slow poke war, so bank the lead in CS and plates instead of forcing a fight he can sustain through.
edits.after: Level 1 is his — Chomp (Q) saps your attack damage every 3.5s and a Pillar (E) angle out-trades your single Noxious Blast before you stack any poison. From level 2 the lane flips to you: prime with Q, then chain Twin Fang (E) off the poison for cheap, near-continuous damage and chip him before Frozen Domain's attack-speed-and-heal zone and his passive regen switch on. Do not over-commit for the kill — his kit is built to out-heal a slow poke war, so buy Grievous Wounds early and bank the lead in CS and plates instead.

edits.before: This is the even stretch. My Twin Fang treadmill out-DPSes him in a pure trade, but he heals it back inside Frozen Domain and never has to disengage — and Pillar of Ice (E) can wall me mid-kite or knock me out of my own retreat line. My Miasma ground is worth less here than against dash bruisers: Trundle has no dash to cancel, so I use W only to slow-zone his approach and buy spacing, not to lock a kill. At 6 my Petrifying Gaze stuns his all-in cold, but respect that Subjugate drains my armor and MR onto him and heals him mid-fight — R to survive the commit and peel, do not flip it into a greedy chase.
edits.after: This is the even stretch. Your Twin Fang treadmill out-DPSes him in a pure trade, but he heals it back inside Frozen Domain and never has to disengage — and Pillar of Ice (E), up every 21s, can wall your kite line or cut your retreat. Miasma's grounding is worth nothing here: Trundle has no dash to shut off and Pillar is terrain, so spend W as a slow zone to buy spacing, not to lock a kill. At 6 Petrifying Gaze stuns his all-in only if he is facing you, and it never stops Subjugate stripping your armor and MR onto him — R to survive and peel, never to chase.

edits.before: This is where I lose the matchup. I stay squishy and short-ranged — no boots, just my passive move speed — while Trundle stacks drain-tank items and Subjugate (R) tears off my resistances, heals him through my entire poison rotation, and lets him simply walk me down. The poke that defined lane stops mattering once he can eat a full Q-W-E and not drop. Close any lead before this: take the early plates, group for objectives on my first-item spike, and never duel him 1v1 once he has two items and his ult up.

edits.before: - Trundle Subjugate: matchup-defining — Steals your resists and HP — never take a long duel into it. Check it before every step-up. - W Miasma is the lifeline; chip damage never gets it. - The ult answers fights, not waves.
edits.after: - Trundle Subjugate: matchup-defining — 120s at rank 1, 80s maxed; never take a long duel into it. - Pillar of Ice is 21s and cuts your kite line. - W Miasma is the lifeline; its grounding does nothing to him, the slow is the point.

notes: Only 20 games in the packet — the smallest sample in my slice, so the 50% figure is soft and I leaned on kit facts and the already-written mirror rather than the win rate. Mirror audits/top/trundle__cassiopeia.json agrees on every mechanical point: grounding is free/worthless because Trundle has no movement abilities, Pillar of Ice cannot be grounded, and Petrifying Gaze's facing rule is the decisive level-6 interaction. The mirror recorded its point 2 as 'correct', so if its chart disagrees with Trundle/Cass/Cass/Skill/Skill/Cass/Trundle, the mirror wins and this should be reconciled. The packet suspect names 'My Twin Fang', 'My Miasma' and 'Frozen Domain' were voice or false-positive issues, not wrong ability names.
